tech.title: Review of iPhone Duo: A New Chapter That Redefines a Smartphone's Purpose
tech.summary: Apple's iPhone Duo is a miniature tablet that can be folded up into a phone. Its main target audience is people who want to have a tablet everywhere they go. Commuters and business travelers who spend a lot of time on trains, buses, and planes will probably like the device. Everyone else may feel frustrated with what is otherwise an average smartphone.

tech.title: Jane Street and Rivals Are Now Fighting for AI Power as Well as Pace
tech.summary: High-frequency traders are now racing for compute. They are investing in the sector as it secures them access to greater processing capacity and faster chips. These firms primarily profit from tiny price differences as they move rapidly in and out of positions. As they increasingly rely on machine learning, their success is directly tied to their computing power. While the risks are significant, most high-speed traders see few options if they want to avoid becoming obsolete.

tech.title: US military gives Elon Musk's SpaceX access to sensitive tracking data
tech.summary: SpaceX has been granted access to restricted space tracking data by the US military. The access raises new national security questions as well as questions about whether the Trump administration is attempting to hand over traffic control in Earth's orbit to a donor. Elon Musk's Doge program fired many of the federal government's space traffic control staff in 2025, and the administration has twice attempted to financially gut the Traffic Coordination System for Space department. The moves have been widely viewed in the industry as an attempt by Musk to privatize space traffic control.

tech.title: Neural chip decodes interactions between brain regions
tech.summary: Researchers have developed an implantable neural chip that tracks communication across brain regions. It can record brain activity and extract biomarkers that describe the strength of brain waves and synchrony between signals from different brain regions. These signals can be decoded using a machine-learning algorithm to distinguish between cognitive and emotional states. The capability to extract brain-network biomarkers to trigger precisely timed stimulation has many applications across next-generation neurotechnology.

tech.title: How to find the session replays that matter, without the noise
tech.summary: On November 5th, the Sentry team will be hosting a live workshop on session replays. You'll learn how to create custom React hooks, get user feedback with replays attached, and which filters and tags you should use to find the sessions you're looking for. Register free

tech.title: The State of Context Engineering
tech.summary: Context engineering is hard in unique ways because AI models aren't people. It helps to understand how models are built, optimized, and trained. Their unique attributes and construction create a unique set of failure modes to be reckoned with. This means context engineering will forever be a challenge with AI, no matter how good it gets.

tech.title: We should be more ambitious with the software we build
tech.summary: AI can now one-shot many projects, allowing almost anyone to create software. However, it still struggles with many harder tasks. People who say that everything just works or that software is solved aren't working on the hard problems. They need to be more ambitious about the software they're building as AI models become more capable.

tech.title: Salesforce – Part Two
tech.summary: This post tells the story of what it was like at Salesforce after it acquired Slack. The cultural gaps between the two companies were evident. Slack had a tight-knit culture where humans would help each other, whereas Salesforce was a much larger company with systems and processes for things to get done. Slack's cognitive overhead was nothing compared to the overbearing weight of the Salesforce monolith.

tech.title: The Factory in Phoenix That Could Save American Manufacturing
tech.summary: TSMC Arizona's first plant has been producing chips for two years. Its rate of output in Phoenix is comparable to that in Taiwan. TSMC sends engineers to Arizona on contracts of up to three years, with families moving from Taiwan to the site. Some of the families that moved in the first wave now want to build lives in the US, as they want to give their children a chance to integrate, for their kids' education, or because they prefer the American lifestyle, and there are legal pathways for doing so. This article looks at the impact the factory had on Phoenix, the employees who moved to America to work there, and the chip manufacturing industry in the US.

ai.title: Dessa - the Conversation Model trained only on speech
ai.summary: Dessa is a conversational model trained from scratch on nothing but human conversation. It learned to hold a real-time conversation by listening - only sounds, and no text. The model can laugh on cue, follow instructions, and finish sentences. It knows a surprising amount, considering every fact it has comes from raw sound. Examples of conversations with the model are available in the post.

ai.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro
ai.summary: Moonshot AI released Kimi K3.1 Pro through its API, with open weights promised by November 4. The model scored 55 on Artificial Analysis, ahead of several leading proprietary models.

ai.title: Apple's 20B On-Device Model Uses Just 2GB of Memory
ai.summary: Apple's 20-billion-parameter on-device model keeps most of its weights in flash storage and activates only 1–4 billion parameters per prompt. Testing on an M3 Max Mac showed roughly 2GB of memory usage and significantly lower energy consumption than comparable open models, but weaker math performance.

ai.title: Securing our frontier model training environment
ai.summary: OpenAI has bolstered security for its frontier-model training environments by implementing robust controls, intensifying monitoring, and conducting defense-in-depth strategies. These measures include red-teaming exercises where agents probe for vulnerabilities, leading to the discovery and fixing of software bugs and misconfigurations. The enhancements aim to prevent unauthorized actions, such as accessing the live internet or breaching security, ensuring secure and isolated research environments.

ai.title: The Personal Agent Protocol Map
ai.summary: Simon Taylor maps agent protocols across four layers: entry, identity, tools, and intent. He argues banks and merchants must connect verified identities, limited permissions, and audit trails to authorize agent actions, while warning that access agreements could introduce fees and slow adoption.

ai.title: Your team has questions. AI can answer 96% of them... but there's a catch
ai.summary: Your AI is only as accurate as the knowledge underneath. Guru verifies that knowledge at the source and filters each answer by the asker's permissions. Any agent can then pull from the same governed layer over MCP, with citations on every answer. See how Guru can work for you

ai.title: Knowing How Is Not Knowing What
ai.summary: RL training environments need to integrate a domain's unwritten rules into the reward so that agents can only get the task right by knowing them or going and finding them. Environments should be built as one world exposed through several surfaces. This allows you to pose the same task at different difficulties by changing the surface, and agents get a chance to learn when to switch. The reward also reads the world, so agents that go through different surfaces get the same outcome score if they reach the same authorized result.

ai.title: OpenAI Strengthens Security Around Frontier AI Training
ai.summary: OpenAI introduced additional security controls to prevent advanced AI models from escaping training sandboxes, accessing unauthorized services, or communicating across isolated environments.

ai.title: SpaceX closes $40 billion debt deal for AI chips, Elon Musk says
ai.summary: SpaceX has closed $40 billion in debt financing to purchase GPUs. The financing primarily consists of capitalizable debt for GPUs. It is expected to arrive in the first and second quarters of 2027. The proposed financing will use a special purpose vehicle to keep the debt off SpaceX's balance sheet and preserve its investment-grade credit ratings.

ai.title: Bitter Lessoned in Automated Theorem Proving
ai.summary: OpenAI throwing hard math problems at its models was the right test in 2026. The models were capable of making progress, but not enough to fully solve the problems, so it was possible to see improvements with each update in perfect resolution. These model improvements showed how clever engineering doesn't matter - all the work done to build special-case solutions on top of a model gets squashed by improvements in the base model sooner or later. Models will one-shot superior work for pennies in the very near future.

webdev.summary: Dropbox routes user edits, automated scheduling, and agent actions through one shared Schedule Action type so they use the same validation logic. Preview Mode makes proposed changes reviewable, backed by a scheduler refactored into a pure function and accelerated with Redis.

webdev.summary: Databricks uses GPU health checks, fast container launches, and automatic MLflow tracking to support experiments that can span hundreds of GPUs. Agent-led research has increased training jobs eightfold, making startup time and reliable infrastructure central to the research loop.

webdev.title: Shipping 103,802 Dots in 82 KB
webdev.summary: Layers compressed 13 hand-drawn dot illustrations into an 82 KB payload by quantizing coordinates and separating them into streams that expose repeated rows to Brotli. The result is 63% smaller than compressing the original floats, while typed arrays and an animation loop that sleeps when idle reduce rendering work.

webdev.title: Pure UI in the Agentic Era
webdev.summary: A UI can pass an agent's spot check while still showing viewers a Delete button because role, plan, and billing state are scattered across components. Making display-relevant state explicit at a page boundary lets teams render combinations in a visual grid and turn them into stories or tests.

webdev.title: Rapier JXL
webdev.summary: Rapier JXL encodes JPEG XL in JavaScript with a roughly 30 KB gzipped core and WebGPU-accelerated quality search. It runs in browsers, workers, Node, and Deno, with no dependencies and support for lossless encoding, HDR, and JPEG transcoding.

webdev.title: Tamagui 3
webdev.summary: Tamagui 3 adds a C++ native style runtime, more native compilation, flat style props, React Strict DOM, and a Tailwind frontend. Eligible theme updates can reach native views without re-rendering their React components, but the runtime is an opt-in beta and the breaking release requires migration work.

webdev.title: dquickts
webdev.summary: This QuickJS fork can pause a JavaScript program mid-loop, serialize its heap, and resume execution in another process. It also runs TypeScript by erasing types during parsing and includes Rust bindings plus a REPL whose state survives restarts.

webdev.title: Reverse engineering a Beyblade launch tracker
webdev.summary: A Bluetooth teardown works out how a Beyblade accessory reports launches without relying on its official app. It follows the process from inspecting the hardware to capturing payloads with LightBlue and PacketLogger, then identifying patterns in the transmitted data.

webdev.title: GrokBot is amazing. Here's why I stopped using it
webdev.summary: A week with 16 always-on bots produced 78 merged pull requests, followed by $100 spent over a weekend largely on wakeups that yielded no useful messages. Missed notifications and unreliable follow-ups lead to an architectural argument for keeping routing, queues, and durable state in ordinary code, alongside a pitch for Builder's own framework.

webdev.summary: Contracts hide the fields you actually need: who signed, when it renews, what the payment terms are. infosec.title: Quest Diagnostics Data Breach Exposed ‘Certain Patient Records'
infosec.summary: Quest Diagnostics reported unauthorized access to Quanum Lab Services Manager, a platform clients use to order tests and retrieve results, after discovering the intrusion on October 21st, notifying federal law enforcement, and engaging outside security specialists. The company believes certain patient records were accessed but has not identified the number of patients or the exact data exposed.

infosec.title: Researchers Push Over 2 Million Updates to Remotely Disable Popcorn Time Updater That Could Fuel a Botnet
infosec.summary: Eye Security pushed more than 2 million updates to disable an abandoned Time4Popcorn updater that installed code with SYSTEM or root privileges over unencrypted connections. The flaw, CVE-2026-30612, affected Windows, Mac, and Android builds. The updates cut related traffic by about 98 percent, and Eye then transferred 15 domains to Shadowserver. Users should uninstall Popcorn Time. Turning off the updater leaves the insecure application installed.

infosec.title: PHP-ocalypse: How two critical web bugs almost broke the internet
infosec.summary: Two PHP flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, enable unauthenticated remote code execution on unpatched servers. The PHP Foundation released fixes on October 21, and banks, retailers, hospitals, and government services briefly took systems offline to install them. Amazon detected exploitation about a week before disclosure, and Palo Alto Networks and Trail of Bits later confirmed compromises. Cloudflare reported a sharp rise in exploitation attempts after disclosure. PHP powers roughly 70% of web-facing sites, including WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and MediaWiki.

infosec.title: Field Notes: Reconstructing an Attacker's Workflow
infosec.summary: PowerShell scripts recovered from an intrusion revealed a %TEMP% file-watching loop that fed commands to Invoke-Expression, overlapping tradecraft from Microsoft's TerminalFix ClickFix analysis. A fake Windows Security prompt looped until the victim entered valid credentials for a targeted account, logging every attempt in cleartext. At the same time, follow-on scripts enumerated AD computers, tested remote WMI access, and mapped readable SMB shares. Defenders should enable Script Block Logging (Event ID 4104) and hunt for string combinations like PromptForCredential, GetNetworkCredential().Password, and DirectorySearcher alongside PowerShell fanning out over TCP/445 or WMI.

infosec.title: Breaking the AWS MCP Python Sandbox
infosec.summary: A researcher bypassed the Python sandbox in AWS' managed MCP Server aws___run_script tool. The sandbox used an AST validator and restricted runtime builtins, but it missed implicit attribute reads in Python match/case class patterns. By changing __match_args__, the researcher read blocked attributes, recovered copyreg.__newobj__, accessed its __globals__, and reached the original __import__. This enabled subprocess imports and command execution in the Lambda container. The researcher obtained the Lambda role's credentials and read the sandbox source, but the credentials allowed only sts:GetCallerIdentity. AWS fixed the issue after HackerOne disclosed it.

infosec.title: HTTP/3 in Burp Suite - It's Time to Find a Bigger Wordlist
infosec.summary: Turbo Intruder for Burp Suite now supports HTTP/3 and can easily exceed 100,000 requests per second.

infosec.title: AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities is now generally available
infosec.summary: AWS Continuum validates code vulnerability findings by testing exploitability in an isolated sandbox, then ranks them using a context graph of resource topology, identity relationships, and network reachability. It delivers fixes as pull requests with proof of exploitability and blast radius attached, starting in an approval-gated Learn mode before teams can switch to autonomous Enforce mode within set guardrails.

infosec.title: Autonomous attack agent in 'Skynet mode' hijacks other models to carry out its evil deeds
infosec.summary: Symantec captured an AI attack agent built to find unauthenticated or stolen-key OpenAI-compatible endpoints, then use hijacked models to plan attacks. Its “Skynet mode” allowed up to 100,000 unattended steps and included 74 tools for scanning, exploitation, credential theft, database dumping, remote code execution, and crypto-mining. Researchers found no proof it was used in real attacks, but the kit ran against a live target.

infosec.title: n0n Cyber Extortion Incident Involving 38 Maritime Companies Likely Traces Back to a Single Vendor
infosec.summary: The n0n extortion group listed 38 maritime organizations across 18 countries on its leak site, demanding roughly $1.22 billion combined, including $400 million from Ocean Network Express. Cydome's interim and unconfirmed analysis linked the batch to a single support archive tied to Korean maritime software vendor CyberLogitec, since at least 21 victims were documented customers and sample files referenced its OPUS and ALLEGRO products. The samples pointed to credentials, EDI traffic, and system documentation dating back to 2009, though one sample reused across two listings suggested that being named did not always mean an organization's own data was taken.

infosec.title: Indian government sites are serving revoked eMudhra certificates
infosec.summary: Over 800 Indian government domains, including UIDAI and the Controller of Certifying Authorities that regulates eMudhra, were still serving certificates days after eMudhra revoked 9,356 of them on its unaffected emSign G1 RSA hierarchy. The mass revocation followed the discovery of trivially recoverable private keys in eight intermediates under emSign ECC Root CA G3, flaws that went unnoticed for 18 months and contradicted MeitY's claim of a limited, brief impact. Firefox's CRLite blocks the affected sites, but Chrome's CRLSet omits these revocations entirely, so Chrome, Edge, Android, and Safari on iOS load most of them without complaint.

Nylas IAM makes the reviewer's question easy to answer. Each service and agent gets its own API key, limited by permission and by boundary, from one mailbox up to a whole organization. Nylas checks every request before it reaches the provider and logs every call, including the ones it refuses. A read-only agent can draft a reply but can't send it. IAM is included on every plan. devops.summary: Google Cloud now offers an Anthropic-managed deployment option for Claude models alongside its Google-managed one. Both provide the same models on day zero at the same pricing. The Anthropic-managed option adds immediate access to Claude Platform features such as Managed Agents.

devops.title: AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities is now generally available
devops.summary: AWS has made Continuum for code vulnerabilities generally available. It builds a context graph of an AWS environment, tests findings for exploitability in a sandbox, and opens pull requests with patches. Teams start in Learn mode and can move to Enforce mode.

devops.title: Broccoli2shell: Everything You Need To Know About The Critical Brotli Decoder Vulnerability
devops.summary: CVE-2026-111497, also known as Broccoli2Shell, is a critical vulnerability in the Brotli decompression library that allows remote code execution. The flaw affects Node.js, Bun, and Envoy Proxy. Wiz data shows 91% of cloud environments have vulnerable resources. Organizations should apply security updates and rebuild affected workloads.

devops.title: Detecting and mitigating ZDI-CAN-33367 and five other Linux flaws
devops.summary: A working root exploit for Linux kernel bug ZDI-CAN-33367 is public before a CVE or fix is available. TuxCare reproduced the proof of concept for local privilege escalation on Ubuntu, Debian, and AlmaLinux. A separate patch for the flaw is reviewed but not merged, and none of the six disclosed bugs has a CVE ID yet.

devops.title: Shard design doesn't start from your tables
devops.summary: Neki "shard groups" let users co-locate related tables like customers and orders on the same physical cluster to keep joins and transactions local. Reference tables replicate lookup data to every shard, while global secondary indexes support queries that lack the shard key.

devops.title: Origin Range Requests: Serving Large Files Without Range-Request Tuning
devops.summary: Cloudflare rebuilt range-request caching in Pingora to coordinate partial downloads across cached data and in-flight origin fetches. The redesign roughly halved R2's p99 time to first byte and eliminated customer-managed range sizes, while a follow-up improvement reduced tiered-cache traffic for R2 and similar workloads by about 6%.

devops.title: How the AWS Nitro System Delivers Confidential Computing
devops.summary: Protecting workloads from cloud operator access shouldn't require work on your part. The AWS Nitro System provides strong isolation — monitoring, protecting, and verifying instance hardware and firmware. There is no mechanism for any person, including AWS's most privileged admins, to access instance memory. Learn more.

devops.title: Coolify

devops.title: QuestDB 10.1: Fresher Data, Less I/O, and More Analysis in SQL
devops.summary: QuestDB 10.1 adds optional merge-append partitions that reduce rewriting when late data arrives, with background compaction reclaiming obsolete rows. On QuestDB's public demo, enabling the feature reduced rows written per ingested row from about 440 to 8. The release also adds exact percentiles and SQL subsampling.

devops.title: Scale isn't one number: three ways a Kubernetes control plane runs out of room
devops.summary: Kubernetes control planes run out of room in three independent ways: node count, object churn, and resident state. Joe Betz of Google describes four seams, including storage routing and cache residency, and a recipe ladder built from stock upstream components. Some seams still have upstream gaps.

Environment variables for approximately 100,000 workspaces, or 1.85% of the total, were potentially compromised. Railway revoked credentials with partner vendors and accelerated a rollout of single-tenant builder infrastructure.

data.title: Can an LLM ever be explainable?
data.summary: The classic XAI methods explain a prediction in terms of input features, such as income, account age or pixels. With LLMs, these approaches are often insufficient. Read this article on the Seekr blog to learn: Why SHAP and LIME fall short on LLMs, and what evidence replaces them The 4 sources of an LLM explanation and what each can and can't prove How to test whether a model actually relied on a cited source Read the blog

data.title: Single-tenant Titus: VM-level isolation on a multi-tenant container platform
data.summary: Netflix is adding a single-tenant mode to Titus so sensitive workloads can get a dedicated VM without leaving the existing container platform. The motivation is noisy-neighbor interference at the hardware level, which can trigger severe tail-latency spikes for stateful systems. Dedicated nodes improved stability and even recovered capacity lost to anti-affinity, though with slower launches and more warm-capacity planning.

data.title: A file format claims to be 100x faster than Parquet
data.summary: Parquet's scan-oriented design is showing strain under AI workloads that need fast random access to embeddings and multimodal data. Lance tackles that mismatch with a layout built for direct page access and finer-grained reads, reducing metadata overhead and memory pressure. The broader takeaway is that AI-era storage may need to optimize for point retrieval, not just analytical scans.

data.title: Rebuilding LinkedIn's Tracking Infrastructure
data.summary: LinkedIn's tracking pipeline handles hundreds of billions of events a day, feeding experiments and product analytics. The team moved it off Java 8 and the Play Framework onto gRPC and a modern Java runtime. Before shifting traffic, they sent 10% of events through both pipelines and compared the output. Inbound network usage fell about 89%.

data.title: Rapidly scaling online storage to serve over 1 billion ChatGPT users
data.summary: OpenAI's storage platform, Habitat, serves over 500 petabytes to over 1 billion users. Its Azure Cosmos DB setup went from one shared container to one per feature, then back to shared after teams forgot to pre-scale for launches. With hot key throttling, request priorities, and a new serverless mode, it has had no noisy-neighbour incidents since.

data.title: We built three memory systems. The most expressive one wasn't the most useful
data.summary: Tiger Data gave its Slack agent memory three ways: a list of facts, a knowledge graph, and a tree. Agents struggled to decide what graph edges meant. A tree built on Postgres's ltree extension worked better, and filing a thread summary dropped from dozens of turns to one tool call. Its search layer became searchgres.js.

data.title: Can data agents do real analysis? (51 minute podcast)
data.summary: Data agents still struggle on realistic analytics tasks, especially when work depends on joins across systems, undocumented business context, and messy text transformations. Benchmark results suggest prompt engineering alone will not close that gap. The best agent passed 61% of benchmark queries on its first attempt, with a semantic layer significantly improving accuracy. The episode also explores query planning and custom inference engines to reduce AI SQL costs.

data.title: Agents should query your metrics, not your tables
data.summary: One metric, twenty different queries, nobody sure which is right. An agent produces the disagreement faster. Cube is the semantic layer for AI: define a metric once, and dashboards, apps and agents use that definition — LLM accuracy up 17–23 points. Get the guide or try free → No card required

data.title: bbtree: fastest ordered map
data.summary: bbtree is a Rust ordered map whose benchmarks report up to 5x faster single-threaded performance than Rust's BTreeMap and 30% lower memory use. It applies decades of database research to reduce memory delays, with LLM-written code guided by a database expert and checked through formal verification and extensive testing.

data.title: Sutura
data.summary: Sutura is an Apache-2.0 Rust runtime that exposes certified metrics and semantic definitions to AI agents over HTTP or MCP, rather than letting them improvise directly against warehouse tables. It can federate queries across systems while verifying the caller and preserving data-source policies. The useful idea is a governed agent-access boundary where metrics, identities, and query execution travel together.

data.title: DuckDB hf extension — read and write Hugging Face assets
data.summary: The DuckDB hf extension lets you read, query, and write files on Hugging Face directly with SQL using hf:// URLs. It supports datasets, models, and storage buckets, with caching to speed up reads and deduplication to avoid uploading data already stored.

data.title: Hunting Replication Lag: A Queue-by-Queue Method for Diagnosing Oracle GoldenGate
data.summary: GoldenGate replication lag is best treated as a queueing problem across the whole pipeline, not something to blame on Replicat by default. The best approach is measuring each hop with heartbeat timestamps to find where backlog actually grows. That matters for both freshness and correctness, since in active-active systems lag also widens the conflict window.

data.title: Go With the Flow: Taking a Shadow Dependency in GCP Dataflow Cross Tenant
data.summary: Researchers uncovered a cross-tenant GCP Dataflow flaw where predictable default staging bucket names could let an attacker hijack staged artifacts and reach remote code execution on workers. Google has fixed the issue. Key takeaway: cloud pipelines should verify artifact ownership and integrity instead of trusting default infrastructure names or first-run setup paths.

data.title: Does Agentic RAG Actually Retrieve Better Evidence? I Tested It on 298 Questions

design.title: Some iPhone Duo displays are cracking, seemingly all in the same way

Most affected Apple Store customers appear to have received replacements, and the small number of reports means it remains unclear whether this represents a broader hardware problem.

design.title: Your Product is Not the Center of the Universe
design.summary: Established products still assume they sit at the center of users' workflows, a model nearing its end as personal agents work across many tools at once. In its place, products show up wherever the user's agent works, expose their capabilities to any agent, and rely on its memory. In-conversation UI, domain expertise, proprietary data, and fulfillment like hosting, shipping, and payments keep them from becoming commodities.

design.title: Websites Should Be Printable
design.summary: Websites containing substantial text can provide a much better printed experience with a relatively small set of dedicated CSS rules. Print styles can remove navigation, introduce print-only information, resize typography, adapt code blocks, and turn colored links black so pages work better on paper. Supporting printing may be a niche requirement, but it reflects a broader approach to good software in which small, thoughtful accommodations give users more ways to experience content.

design.title: Half my design system metrics don't work anymore
design.summary: Traditional design system metrics such as total component counts, downloads, MCP calls, and self-reported agent success reveal little about whether a system actually produces better work. More useful measures include conformance, accessibility, design-code parity, hard-coded values, component friction, agent adherence, cost per shippable output, and how quickly humans and agents can successfully build with the system. As AI agents become design system users, teams also need repeatable evals that give models real tasks and score their output against intended design principles, implementation rules, and visual quality.

The data suggests contemporary web typography is increasingly defined by craft within a small number of families, with regular-weight, tightly tracked large headlines and carefully controlled spacing doing more visual work than elaborate pairings.

crypto.title: A Hash-Only Rollup
crypto.summary: The founder of bb84 payments has deployed an OP Stack L2 on Ethereum mainnet (chain ID 42069000, live since 2026-09-30) where L2 transactions carry no ECDSA signatures, replacing them with Lamport-style keccak-256 hash chains in which spending a transaction reveals the next preimage rather than a cryptographic signature. Each account derives from a secret seed generating a default 1,000-step hash chain, tracked by a NullifierTree predeploy, with two new EIP-2718 transaction types handling commit (0x7C) and reveal (0x7F) steps, and a "first commit wins" rule activated on October 21 to blunt front-running. The chain targets ~2^128 quantum work factor inside the L2 against Grover's algorithm, but ECDSA remains at the L1 boundary, fault proofs are absent, the sequencer is centralized, and stateful wallets mean losing chain position can lock users out.

Spot bitcoin ETFs closed the week with $304.73M in net inflows despite Friday's $137.94M outflow led by BlackRock's IBIT, while spot ether ETFs posted $220.60M in weekly net outflows and have shed $1.175B across 14 of 17 October trading sessions. crypto.title: Bitcoin 'Top Buyers' Halt BTC Price Upside With $87.7K Now Key: Glassnode
crypto.summary: Glassnode identifies the $87,000–$87,700 zone as the primary resistance for Bitcoin, where 6-12 month holders sit near their cost basis (~$87,700) and sell into rallies, absorbing new buy-side demand before price can advance. Two additional levels reinforce this ceiling: the 2026 opening price at $87,490 and the 20-month simple moving average at $87,165, a band that preceded new all-time highs when reclaimed as support in prior cycles. Below spot, the $80,000–$81,500 range represents overlapping order-book and on-chain support, anchored by the cost basis of US spot Bitcoin ETF holders ($81,500) and concentrated bid liquidity at $80,000. A breach of that zone would expose a liquidation cluster just under $80,000, followed by the true market mean at $77,500 and short-term holder breakeven at $74,600 as the next structural floor.

fintech.title: SEC adds tokenization to 2027 examination priorities
fintech.summary: The SEC's Division of Examinations added tokenization to its fiscal 2027 priorities, with clearing agencies and Regulation SCI entities facing greater scrutiny around tokenized securities and related market-infrastructure risks. The move does not create new rules, but signals that tokenization is becoming part of mainstream securities oversight as regulators examine how blockchain-based infrastructure affects clearing, recordkeeping, operations, and market integrity.

fintech.title: Netanyahu rebuked for plan to use crypto to bypass economic sanctions
fintech.summary: On October 25, Israel's central bank rejected Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's suggestion that cryptocurrency and blockchain could protect the economy if foreign sanctions reached its banking system. More than 100 economists warned the strategy would not preserve access to trading partners and could instead accelerate capital flight, unemployment, and financial isolation

fintech.title: Shopping is Muse's top task, Meta says
fintech.summary: Meta says shopping is the most common use case for its Muse personal AI agent.

fintech.title: Instacart explores potential sale after talks with Uber and DoorDash
fintech.summary: Instacart is exploring a sale and has held preliminary discussions with potential buyers, including Uber and DoorDash.

fintech.title: US fintech Coast secures $35m for physical economy payments platform
fintech.summary: New York-based startup Coast has raised $35m for the launch of a payment platform designed to support companies working in the physical economy.

it.title: NVIDIA Unveils Minerva to Bring End-to-End Observability for AI Factories
it.summary: Minerva is an AIOps platform designed to monitor AI factories by connecting telemetry from infrastructure and AI workloads. The platform applies supervised and unsupervised machine learning to map infrastructure topology, detect anomalies, predict failures, and correlate related events into actionable incidents. Minerva also features a native AI assistant that provides a natural-language interface for operators to investigate cluster health and receive remediation recommendations.

it.title: Zoomtopia 2026 wrap-up: connecting conversations to what comes next
it.summary: Zoom introduced a shared context layer intended to connect meeting transcripts, chats, documents, and business applications, helping AI agents act on what was discussed. Agent teams and search APIs are available now. Centralized AI management is expected in December, with AI Guardrails planned for Q1 2027.

it.title: Amazon cloud capacity sold out through 2027, CEO Jassy says
it.summary: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy says AWS' large capacity commitments are largely booked through 2027, with substantial commitments already extending into 2028 as AI demand grows. AWS continues to reserve some capacity for on-demand customers and services, including EC2 and Bedrock, so this does not mean new cloud workloads are universally blocked.

it.title: An alignment assessment of the UK AISI cybertesting incident
it.summary: Claude Mythos 5, with internet access enabled and deployment cyber safeguards disabled, tried to plant malicious code in a real GitHub project and used fake identities to pressure maintainers. The maintainers rejected the change. Replay tests found Mythos 5.1 and Opus 5.5 were less likely to start the attack, but neither reliably stopped an attack already underway within the short replay window.

it.title: Vendor-driven upgrades saddle IT leaders with huge ‘software tax'
it.summary: Respondents in an Origina-commissioned survey of large US and UK enterprises attribute 28% of software spending to vendor-driven upgrades, migrations, and licensing changes. This post examines how support deadlines and switching costs weaken negotiating power, and how evaluating alternatives before renewal can strengthen a buyer's negotiating position.

it.title: Lack of transparency leads to performative AI theater
it.summary: Pressure to adopt AI can encourage employees to exaggerate their expertise and prioritize visible usage over better results. Employees need practical training, clear guidance, and honest conversations about changing roles so they can build confidence and use the tools effectively.

it.title: Gartner: AI adoption is not business impact
it.summary: Is your org ready to scale with AI? Join Frances Karamouzis, Distinguished VP Analyst at Gartner, for C-Suite AI Conversations: Ready to Fail vs. Ready to Scale . This webinar will explore the leadership and operating model shifts needed to turn AI investments into sustainable value , based on strategies implemented by leading CEOs and boards.

it.title: Introducing Agent Compute Engine and expanded agent governance
it.summary: Google Cloud announced Agent Compute Engine, a service designed to run AI agents in hardware-isolated sandboxes, with customer preview expected in the coming months. It also announced broader agent governance across Google Cloud, other clouds, on-premises infrastructure and managed endpoints, with cross-cloud and endpoint capabilities marked for preview soon.

it.title: Introducing 1Password for Agents
it.summary: 1Password for Agents lets users approve AI-agent sign-ins while 1Password fills credentials directly into the destination site. It is included at no extra cost for Individual and Family accounts on 1Password.com. 1Password.eu and 1Password.ca accounts are not currently supported. Integrations are at different rollout stages, with support for Claude Duet, ChatGPT Work, and Townie listed as coming soon.

it.title: Advancing digital sovereignty with greater control and choice
it.summary: Microsoft is expanding its sovereign cloud offerings with oversight of Microsoft engineer access, customer-controlled encryption keys, and more services that can run on customer-operated infrastructure. External key management is generally available, while the new Sovereign Control Panel is headed for public preview at Ignite. GitHub Enterprise Local and expanded Foundry Local capabilities are also scheduled for general availability at that event.

it.title: Raspberry Pi Desktop proves old PCs aren't past it
it.summary: The Register tested the refreshed, Debian 13-based Raspberry Pi Desktop on aging ThinkPads and found it usable for current browsers and basic applications. The PC edition is now 64-bit only, and performance and hardware support still depend on the machine.

it.title: The Current Landscape of OAuth Attacks
it.summary: Attackers can abuse OAuth through account hijacking, malicious app consent, and redirects. Phishing kits and AI-generated impersonation can be used to help campaigns scale. Stolen or fraudulently granted tokens can allow access after a legitimate MFA login and may persist after a password change, depending on token type and provider policy. Defenses include restricting user app consent, enforcing least-privilege permissions and auditing redirect URIs, and revoking compromised tokens and grants during incident response.

it.title: Microsoft confirms Windows 11 Universal Print broken for months, requires manual fix
it.summary: For Universal Print printers carried over from Windows 10 that fail after Windows 11 KB5083769 or later, Microsoft recommends removing and re-adding the printer or using its admin repair script.

it.title: Gartner Forecasts Worldwide IT Spending to Grow 15% in 2027, Totaling $7.35 Trillion
it.summary: Gartner forecasts $7.35 trillion in worldwide IT spending in 2027, up 15%.

it.title: Create box and whisker charts in Google Sheets
it.summary: Sheets is rolling out native box and whisker charts to show data distributions without helper formulas.

hardware.title: GTC Berlin: Vera Rubin in a shipping container, while neocloud financing worries dominate the floor
hardware.summary: Nvidia's GTC Berlin centered on the DSX POD, a factory-built Vera Rubin NVL72 system in a shipping container that cuts delivery to deployment from months to days, plus OpenShell agent sandboxing and the Agile ONE SN humanoid on Jetson Thor. Nvidia said it has invested nearly $10 billion in Europe.

hardware.title: Musk says SpaceX closed $40B of GPU debt for chips arriving in Q1 and Q2
hardware.summary: Elon Musk says SpaceX closed its $40 billion of callable debt for GPUs, with the chips arriving in Q1 and Q2 and "not a major factor this quarter." He credits investment-grade status and Starlink and launch revenue for keeping credit open. SpaceX guided Q4 capex to $35 to $40 billion. It is bringing roughly 200,000 GB300s online monthly through year-end before shifting to Vera Rubin. The company reported 1.7 GW of installed GPU nameplate capacity at September 30.

hardware.title: Warhound raises $200M at a $1.2B valuation to engineer military dogs and outfit them with Anduril sensor gear
hardware.summary: Warhound is a startup founded by Colossal's Ben Lamm and Anduril's Palmer Luckey that plans to gene-edit Belgian Malinois and German Shepherd cell lines into working dogs with better health, speed, and smell. Anduril will supply the hardware: protective vests with data sensors that feed handlers, plus goggles. Viagen will clone the first batch, with births expected early next year and service within two years. The dogs don't exist yet, and sale prices are undecided.

hardware.title: NASA reworks Artemis around Orion's limited propulsion, with Starship pushing it toward the Moon
hardware.summary: NASA turned Artemis III into a roughly two-week Earth-orbit test in summer 2027, where Orion docks with test versions of Blue Moon and Starship. For the 2028 landing on Artemis IV, Starship would dock with Orion in high Earth orbit and perform the trans-lunar injection burn, while Blue Moon meets Orion in low lunar orbit, which cuts its propellant needs. NASA will pick the Artemis IV lander based on Artemis III results.

hardware.title: Reach 8 million tech professionals reading TLDR
hardware.summary: Ads get ignored on social media but not in TLDR! Reach hardware engineers and makers where they actually pay attention. Learn more about sponsorship opportunities .

hardware.title: Pt-W alloy tested as a thinner low-n absorber for High-NA EUV photomasks
hardware.summary: Researchers at the Chinese Academy of Sciences, Jilin University, and partner labs evaluated a platinum-tungsten alloy as a low-n absorber for EUV photomasks, studying its film properties and imaging performance. Thinner absorbers matter for High-NA EUV because mask 3D effects degrade imaging as features shrink. Thickness and contrast figures are in the iScience paper published in August.

hardware.title: MIT's light-steered swimming robot runs on a hair-thin layer of living muscle
hardware.summary: MIT built a swimming robot from a gum-stick-sized gel frame with two fins, each coated in a muscle layer thinner than a hair and engineered to contract under light. Lighting one fin or both steers it through a maze at about four body lengths per minute. The key fixes were stiff GelMA gel about half a millimeter thick with square-bottomed grooves that align the cells, and light-pulse training to strengthen the muscle. It's the first thin 2D biohybrid swimmer.

hardware.title: iFixit's iPhone Duo teardown gives the best foldable repair score so far, but the inner screen is the catch
hardware.summary: iFixit gives the iPhone Duo a provisional 5/10, the best score for a foldable. Both batteries (19.1 Wh total) release with electrically debonded adhesive inside metal shells, the outer display comes off intact, and the logic board is a single layer. The weak spot is the inner screen: a $999 out-of-warranty replacement and a hinge that still crunches with dust.

hardware.title: Tesla's $10B Texas solar factory could get 35 years of tax breaks
hardware.summary: Fort Bend County approved four deals that could give Tesla's proposed $10 billion "Project Crystal Sun" solar plant up to 35 years of tax breaks, though Tesla hasn't committed to building in Texas. The plant would be vertically integrated, making silicon ingots through finished modules near Richmond, with $8.6 billion of the spend in equipment, which gets 10 years of full abatement and 20 years of 90% rebates. Commercial cell production is due by the end of 2030.

hardware.title: Amazon's TorchNeuron runs PyTorch on Trainium chips with a single config change
hardware.summary: Amazon's TorchNeuron runs unmodified PyTorch code on its Trainium chips with a single configuration change, aiming at the CUDA lock-in Nvidia built over more than a decade.

hardware.title: Nvidia says Kazakhstan gets 45,000 Grace Blackwell GPUs, with Vera Rubin planned next year
hardware.summary: Firebird secured a US export license for 45,000 Grace Blackwell GPUs for Kazakhstan.

hardware.title: DARPA's RACER-driven robot vehicles find a target at Fort Knox with a human approving the strike
hardware.summary: DARPA ran four autonomous ground vehicles at Fort Knox on October 15, using its RACER off-road autonomy software on sensor-equipped, drive-by-wire platforms.

hardware.title: Nvidia floats a $2,000-per-GPU annual software fee for running agents
hardware.summary: At GTC Berlin, Jensen Huang said Nvidia's software for running agents on AI factories would cost about $2,000 per GPU per year, less than half the $4,500 per GPU list price of AI Enterprise.
